identity.name: Sodium ethyl p-hydroxybenzoate
synonyms: p-Hydroxybenzoic acid ethyl ester sodium salt

function.mechanism: Parabens inhibit growth of yeasts, molds and some bacteria, largely through membrane/enzyme disruption; activity is stronger in acidic foods.

adi.basis: Temporary group ADI for the sum of methyl and ethyl p-hydroxybenzoic acid esters and their sodium salts.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA AFC panel considered para-hydroxybenzoates (E214-219) safe at current use levels, with a temporary group ADI; propyl and butyl were not supported for inclusion in that group ADI because of juvenile-rat reproductive findings.

fda.cfr_citation: No direct listing for sodium ethyl p-hydroxybenzoate in current Title 21 eCFR full text (snapshot 2026-02-25); related parabens listed at 21 CFR 184.1490, 184.1670, 582.3490, 582.3670.

adi.basis: Group ADI for methyl and ethyl esters of p-hydroxybenzoic acid; JECFA comment notes propyl exclusion from the group ADI in 2006.

concerns.summary: Recent observational studies report associations between urinary ethylparaben and metabolic/endocrine endpoints (obesity, MASLD, thyroid-related outcomes), while causality remains unproven.
High-dose oral animal studies reported reproductive effects (implantation/decidualization) for ethylparaben exposure in mice.
Mouse data suggest chronic methyl/ethyl paraben exposure may worsen high-fat-diet NAFLD through microbiome-linked lipid pathway changes.

no_concern_confirmed: No specific IARC monograph classification was identified for ethylparaben/sodium ethyl p-hydroxybenzoate.
A Taiwanese population probabilistic assessment reported paraben hazard indices below 1 in that dataset (PMID: 41164939).

populations: High cumulative consumers of processed foods
Children and adolescents in higher-exposure settings
Populations in regions with high measured food paraben concentrations
adi_exceedance.notes: A 2025 global scoping review reported EU food concentrations generally within limits but highlighted potential cumulative ADI exceedance and much higher concentrations in some non-EU datasets (PMID: 41172944).

risk_assessment.rationale: E215 sits in an ADI-based regulatory framework but with caveats (temporary/group ADI context and related-paraben exclusions). Newer literature shows credible endocrine/metabolic signals and possible exceedance in some subgroups, but no major carcinogenic classification or broad food ban was identified.
key_factors: EFSA temporary group ADI context for E214-219 (2004)
No direct Title 21 eCFR listing found for sodium ethyl p-hydroxybenzoate
Evidence of potential cumulative exposure exceedance in some settings
